title: Kochen-Specker Configurations from Grids on Dual Quadrics
abstract: We develop a geometric framework for constructing and organizing Kochen--Specker configurations in real four-dimensional space. The construction uses finite grids on pairs of smooth quadrics related by Euclidean polarity. Their incidence geometry directly produces orthogonal measurement contexts and parity proofs of quantum contextuality, yielding infinite families of configurations and a geometric interpretation and extension of a previously known cyclic construction. For a distinguished subfamily, the same geometry admits a canonical completion determined by secant lines. The first two instances of this completion recover the exceptional root configurations of types $F_4$ and $H_4$, while the smallest case also recovers the Cabello configuration and its embedding in the Peres configuration. Thus several prominent four-dimensional contextual configurations, previously obtained from different constructions, arise from a single projective-geometric mechanism.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, unified projective-geometric method using grids on dual quadrics to systematically construct Kochen-Specker configurations. It shows that this single mechanism can generate numerous known examples of quantum contextuality, including those related to $F_4$ and $H_4$. The work provides deep mathematical insight into the structure of quantum contextuality.
main_problem: The paper develops a systematic geometric framework to construct and organize Kochen-Specker (KS) configurations, which are mathematical realizations of quantum contextuality.
main_result: It demonstrates that several prominent contextual configurations (like those related to $F_4$ and $H_4$) arise from a single, unified projective-geometric mechanism involving grids on dual quadrics in $\mathbb{P}^3(\mathbb{R})$.
method: The construction uses finite grids on pairs of smooth quadrics related by Euclidean polarity, employing a 'polar-secant principle' to generate orthogonal measurement contexts.
model_or_system: The model is quantum contextuality, mathematically represented by sets of rays (vectors) in a Hilbert space that must satisfy specific constraints (contextuality) regardless of the measurement context chosen.
key_observables: Orthogonal contexts (sets of four pairwise orthogonal rays), the existence of infinite families of KS configurations, and the recovery of known exceptional root configurations ($F_4, H_4$).
important_parameters: Odd integers $p, q \geq 3$ used to define the grid parameters $Z_{p,q}$.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the properties of Euclidean polarity and the parity criterion for KS configurations; later sections test assumptions about complete intersections in projective space.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the structure involves geometric constructions on quadrics and verification of algebraic relationships.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general geometric framework (quadrics and polarity) to construct an infinite family of configurations ($Z_{p,q}$), then analyzes specific cases (Cabello, $F_4, H_4$), and finally verifies advanced structural properties using computational algebra (e.g., checking for complete intersections).
why_interesting: While highly mathematical, the core subject—quantum contextuality—is fundamental to quantum foundations and has implications for understanding measurement limitations in quantum information theory.
